title: How do we cut an angle into two equal parts?
description: Any angle X O Y is bisected with a ruler and a compass, and the two parts are shown to be equal. Equal marks on both arms and equal arcs from them meet at a point on the bisector. Keeko's doubt, that a bigger arc from one mark will do, is tested and struck out.
teaching_notes: One idea: two points the same distance from O on the arms, then equal arcs from them, give two congruent triangles by SSS. Watch for students who use different radii for the two arcs.

source: Draw any angle ∠XOY. Bisect it using only a ruler and a comp
video_script.why: The child can build a right angle but has not yet cut a given angle into two equal parts.
video_script.substitution: Two equal marks on the arms and two equal arcs from them give two triangles with three pairs of equal sides, so the angles at O are equal.
video_script.anchor: An angle X O Y: bisect it using only a ruler and a compass, and justify that the two parts are equal.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko draws a small arc from A and a bigger arc from B. The arcs cross at a point that is not the same distance from A and B, so the triangles cannot match.
video_script.payoff_line: The line O C bisects the angle X O Y

final_answer.value: OC bisects ∠XOY, because ΔOAC ≅ ΔOBC by SSS
final_answer.spoken: the line O C bisects the angle X O Y, because the triangles O A C and O B C are congruent by side side side

never_show: the line OC before step three
maths_rules: An arc with centre O cuts OY at A and OX at B: OA = OB.
Arcs of one radius from A and from B, long enough to meet inside the angle, meet at C: AC = BC.
In triangles OAC and OBC: OA = OB, AC = BC, OC common, so triangle OAC is congruent to triangle OBC by SSS.
So angle AOC = angle BOC, and OC bisects angle XOY.
Slip: radii r from A and R from B with R more than r meet at a point C with AC = r and BC = R, so AC is not equal to BC and the triangles do not match.
video_script.design: One idea: equal marks on the arms, equal arcs from them, and SSS. The angle X O Y stays the whole video. Keeko's doubt is a bigger arc from B.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, put the compass point on O, and draw an arc across both arms.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Name the cut on O Y as eigh, and the cut on O X as B.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>O eigh equals O B, as both are radii of one arc.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, open the compass long enough for two arcs to meet. Draw an arc inside the angle from eigh.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Keep the same radius, and draw an arc from B.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The arcs meet at C, so eigh C equals B C.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, look at triangles O eigh C and O B C.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>O eigh equals O B, eigh C equals B C, and O C is common. By side side side, they are congruent.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Then angle eigh O C equals angle B O C.
